properties.headline: Extreme Heat Watch issued June 19 at 9:27PM MST until June 23 at 7:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible below 4000 feet, with
daytime temperatures ranging from 97 degrees at Havasupai Gardens,
to 111 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This watch is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures could rise to dangerous levels.

miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM NOON TO 7 PM MDT SATURDAY

PLATEAU, WEST CENTRAL AND NORTH CENTRAL MOUNTAINS, AND THE UPPER RIO
GRANDE AND LOWER CHAMA RIVER VALLEYS...

.Very dry air will enter northwestern New Mexico on Saturday, with
many areas seeing 6 to 12 hours of single digit relative humidity.
Winds strengthening to 15 to 25 mph, deep atmospheric mixing, and
very dry fuels will increase the risk of rapid fire spread.

Mountains (Zone 105), North Central Mountains (Zone 120), and Upper
Rio Grande Valley and Lower Chama River Valley (Zone 121).

* TIMING...From noon to 7 PM MDT Saturday.

* 20 FOOT WINDS...West winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative humidity between 5 to 10 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued June 20 at 10:23AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
As Tropical Storm Mekkhala (07W) continues to strengthen, a monsoon
trough that has developed over the last 24 hours, will remain in
place. Deep moisture transport in the west to southwesterly flow and
favorable lift (aided by orographical lift, especially in Koror and
northern Palau), will remain conducive to a heavy rainfall
environment. Rain rates in excess of 1.5 inches per hour could
develop from time to time. Total rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches,
with localized amounts near 8 inches, are possible through Tuesday
morning. This could result in some localized flooding and mudslide
concerns, especially for Koror and northern portions of the Republic
of Palau. Wind gusts to 35 mph (possibly higher) may accompany the
heavier showers or thunderstorms that develop. Folks are urged to
stay informed via the local weather offices in Palau and Yap, as well
as with the NWS Guam Forecast office.

properties.areaDesc: Chuuk Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued June 20 at 10:23AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Chuuk remains situated between Tropical Storm Mekkhala, which is
well north of Yap/west of Guam, and Invest 93W which is located just
west/northwest of Pohnpei. A NET (Near-Equatorial Trough) connecting
the two systems runs through Chuuk. This provides sufficient lift
and moisture conducive to locally heavy showers at any time. With
that said, the "better" potential for heavier rainfall will depend on
how quickly Invest 93W strengthens and where it tracks. The general
expectation is for a slowly-organizing system to track towards the
Marianas over the next week, with this system perhaps starting to
organize more north of Chuuk in 48 hours. As it does so, a "monsoon-
like" southwesterly flow may develop. At this time, rainfall amounts
of 2 to 4 inches, with localized amounts to 6 inches are possible,
which could cause some minor flooding or mudslide concerns. Again,
the most likely time for this to occur would be during the next 72
hours (through Tuesday morning).

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued June 19 at 3:26PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has extended an air quality alert due
to harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...Boyle Heights and East Los Angeles. Levels of particle
pollution can vary by time and location depending on emissions and
local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 1:00 PM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
